title: Austin Tackles Growth, Noise, Bus Fares
summary:
*   **Urban Development Boom:** Approved significant rezonings, converting several residential areas to general retail, commercial, and office districts, notably impacting the Burnet Road corridor and other growing sections of the city.
*   **City Limits Expand:** Initiated the annexation process for over 70 acres of land, incorporating new subdivisions like Highland Hills and Allandale West into the city's boundaries.
*   **Bus Fare Adjustments:** Advanced an ordinance to its final reading that would modify public bus fares and the payment structure for local transit operators.
*   **Public Safety & Noise Enforcement:** Responded to citizen complaints by announcing stricter enforcement of the muffler ordinance to curb "unnecessary motor noises" and promote road safety, especially for school children. The Mayor also urged residents to register and vaccinate their dogs for public health.

MR. A. B. ROSSON appeared in the interest of the Dog ordinance, and reporting a dog in his
neighborhood running loose most of thetime. He submitted a petition asking that the
Council do something to furnish relief from the unnecessary motor noises. Councilman
Pearson stated there was an ordinance covering this noise. The Mayor announced that
publicity be given to the public that the muffler ordinance was going to be enforced, that
with the 25,000 school children and the necessity of safe driving, that this ordinance
must be enforced more gigidly. He asked the Press, Radio and T.V. to carry the publicity
also.
The Mayor asked that the people be asked to register their dogs for their own protection,
and that they have the dogs vaccinated, as the danger was just as great when they were
tied up as if they were running loose. It was suggested that the Veterinarians continue
sending their notices to the people about the time for vaccinations for the animals.
Councilman Pearson had a report from the Trinity Laboratories on the gravel from the pit
of Pat Canion. Councilman Pearson suggested setting the standards whereby both the sand
and the crushed stone could both be used. The matter was referred to the City Manager to
see if it met the requirements, and to bring back a report next Thursday.
There being no further business the Council adjourned at 11:30 Α.Μ. subject to the call of
the Mayor.
